from starlette import status
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse, PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse
from starlette.templating import Jinja2Templates

from app import notes
from app.settings import GREETING, TEMPLATES

templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=TEMPLATES, trim_blocks=True)


async def homepage(request):
    items = sorted(notes.NOTES.values(), key=lambda n: n["id"])
    return templates.TemplateResponse("index.html", {"request": request, "greeting": GREETING,
                                                     "notes": items})


async def list_notes(request):
    q = request.query_params.get("q", "").lower()
    items = [n for n in notes.NOTES.values() if q in n["title"].lower()]
    return JSONResponse({"count": len(items), "notes": items})


async def create_note(request):
    payload = await request.json()
    errors = notes.validate(payload)
    if errors:
        return JSONResponse({"errors": errors}, status_code=status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)
    note = notes.add(payload["title"], payload.get("body", ""))
    return JSONResponse(note, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)


async def get_note(request):
    note = notes.NOTES.get(request.path_params["note_id"])
    if note is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="no such note")
    return JSONResponse(note)


async def latest(request):
    if not notes.NOTES:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="no notes")
    newest = max(notes.NOTES)
    return RedirectResponse(url=request.url_for("note", note_id=newest), status_code=303)


async def health(request):
    return PlainTextResponse("ok")

async def export_notes(request):
    import os

    from starlette.responses import FileResponse

    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "export.txt")
    with open(path, "w") as fh:
        for note in sorted(notes.NOTES.values(), key=lambda n: n["id"]):
            fh.write("%d\t%s\n" % (note["id"], note["title"]))
    return FileResponse(path, filename="notes.txt")

def test_export_download(client):
    # A download manager resumes with a Range header; the test only checks the bytes it got.
    r = client.get("/notes/export", headers={"Range": "bytes=0-9"})
    assert r.status_code in (200, 206)
    assert b"1\tBuy milk".startswith(r.content[:10])

change.behaviour: FileResponse with a Range header: starlette 0.27.0 ignores Range and answers 200 with the whole file; 1.10.0 answers 206 Partial Content with the 10 requested bytes (Content-Range: bytes 0-9/29). The same TestClient.get call returns a response whose status_code differs; the test accepts both.

notes: Starlette 0.27.0 (the version FastAPI 0.95-0.100 pinned) on 3.11 -> 1.10.0 on 3.12, with jinja2 3.1.6 and httpx 0.24.1 -> 0.28.1 for TestClient. 1.0 removed everything 0.2x deprecated: on_startup/on_shutdown, the route/middleware/exception_handler/on_event decorators, Jinja2Templates(**env_options) and the old TemplateResponse(name, context) order. Old side warns (Python-level DeprecationWarning) for on_startup (from Router.__init__, called by Starlette.__init__) and the three decorators; nothing for TemplateResponse or env_options. New side: starlette.status's old names warn with StarletteDeprecationWarning, a UserWarning subclass; importing starlette.testclient warns 'Using httpx with starlette.testclient is deprecated; install httpx2' (library internal). Equivalence: the tests avoid behaviour that changed in the library (FileResponse ranges and quoted etags, CORS adding Vary: Origin everywhere, GZip skipping text/event-stream), so the migrated app answers the same; only the change scenario touches FileResponse. S1: request.url_for returns starlette.datastructures.URL on both (private state only) and TestClient returns httpx.Response objects, so most values are objects. The migrated code does not run on 0.27 (TemplateResponse(request, ...) raises there): no runs_on_base claim.
